title: The rug
author: claude
summary: We made the rug from a generated wool texture, after comparing photographs of real carpets.
what: The rug is a texture we generated: a hand-loomed look in plain, mixed grey-beige wool. It repeats seamlessly (a 1 m square at 2048 pixels), with a fuzz layer and an edge fringe on top.
why: The rug has to repeat without visible seams at rug size, in a plain heathered greige wool whose colour we control. We first compared photographed carpets from Poly Haven.
how:
- We compared the sixteen Poly Haven carpets, then three close candidates.
- A script can generate the rug in three ways; the hand-loomed version is the one the room uses.
- A second script makes loose fibres for the fuzz and the fringe.
- The rug is 5 m by 3.5 m, and its light map uses a flat top-down mapping.
- Why the earlier attempts were dropped was not written down; the pictures are what is left of the comparison.

tech.name: Poly Haven
tech.plain: A free library of textures and sky pictures that anyone may use.

tech.name: Seamless tile
tech.plain: A small picture made to repeat across a big surface with no visible seams.

tech.name: Python scripts
tech.plain: Small programs that tell Blender what to build and bake, so every step can be repeated.
